text.tspan: Annual Report of the Great Lakes Regional Water Use Database Representing 2023 Water Use Data
Approximately 80% of New York state’s fresh surface water, over 700 miles of shoreline, and nearly 48%
of New York’s land area are contained in the watersheds of Lake Erie, Lake Ontario and the St. Lawrence
River—including the Lake Champlain and Lake George watersheds. More than four million New Yorkers
depend on the fresh water of these watersheds for drinking water.
Excluding in-stream hydroelectric water use (2,178,908 mgd or 8,248,064 mld),
withdrawals from the basin for New York totaled 3,235 mgd (12,244 mld) in 2023, representing a less than
1% decrease from 2022 withdrawals (3,262 mgd or 12,349 mld). New York facilities withdrew the most
water from the Lake Ontario watershed, making up 86% of New York’s total withdrawal from the basin at
. New York water withdrawals by sector over the past five years (excluding in-stream hydroelectric
Great Lakes Basin Advisory Council. 2010. Our Great Lakes Water Resources: Conserving and Protecting Our Water Today for Use Tomorrow
Because of an updated calculation method, withdrawals for in-stream hydroelectric power production in New York will appear to be much higher
in 2023 than in previous years. In 2022, this value should be 2,133,792 mgd rather than 218,816 mgd as was reported in the 2022 Annual Report.
